outcome: Implemented capabilities are origin-neutral across canonical metadata and authoring bindings
owner_impact: Capabilities that predate the AI request workflow and capabilities later discovered through research AI now follow the same canonical implementation contract once implemented: complete verified implementation metadata, publication provenance, and a mandatory deployed authoring binding. Neutral discovery refuses inconsistent capability truth instead of silently treating old and new capabilities differently.

next.text: #335 must now be rerun read-only against the exact #354 production candidate. #336 remains unstarted until that re-audit is green.

technical_evidence: The 11 pre-registry implemented capabilities are backfilled to the exact #348 production-verification baseline git:10bdfe63a9af0c3eedc4896682fda7bfddf71d89 at 2026-09-19T05:58:01Z rather than inventing historical request/GitHub lineage.
A database constraint requires every implemented canonical capability to have non-empty implementation contracts, implementation_version and implemented_at.
The canonical registry read seam exposes implementation_version and implemented_at alongside identity/state/contracts/provenance.

Neutral MCP discovery validates the live canonical registry against deployed authoring bindings: implemented rows require bindings and complete metadata/provenance; bindings to missing or non-implemented rows are rejected.
Non-implemented canonical capabilities remain valid without authoring bindings, preserving the Professor-approved-before-implementation lifecycle.
MCP server/interface are 3.7.0/13; authoring contract remains vlab.authoring/0.7 and capability-request interface remains vlab.capability-request/4.
No simulator/kernel/physics, observation/action/runtime, authoring syntax, Experiment artifact/interface, role/triage authority, CI/CD or deployment-workflow behavior is changed.
